body:
Notes from @yusong-yan on which stacks (determined using yb-prof.py memory profiling) corresponded to the ones with the memory leak:

> So far, what I found is that the memory generated from
> 
> yb::tserver::PgClientServiceImpl::Heartbeat()
> std::__1::__function::__func<>::operator()()
> yb::tserver::PgClientServiceIf::Handle()
> yb::rpc::ServicePoolImpl::Handle()
> yb::rpc::InboundCall::InboundCallTask::Run()
> yb::rpc::(anonymous namespace)::Worker::Execute()
> yb::Thread::SuperviseThread()
> start_thread

> and

> yb::tserver::PgClientSession::EnsureSession()
> /yb::tserver::PgClientSession::BeginTransactionIfNecessary()
> yb::tserver::PgClientSession::SetupSession()
> yb::tserver::PgClientSession::Perform()
> yb::tserver::PgClientServiceImpl::Perform()
> std::__1::__function::__func<>::operator()()
> yb::tserver::PgClientServiceIf::Handle()
> yb::rpc::ServicePoolImpl::Handle()
> yb::rpc::InboundCall::InboundCallTask::Run()
> yb::rpc::(anonymous namespace)::Worker::Execute()
> yb::Thread::SuperviseThread()
> start_thread


> caused the total memory to slowly grow while workload is running. Essentially, they are many PgClientSession objects, and also YBSession  objects created by PgClientSession::EnsureSession() . Memory growth is slow. For example, for PgClientSession, about 30MB grow in 50 min, but the memory usage never dropped as long as the workload is still running (even I saw there is expiration mechanism for each session in pg_client_service.cc).

body:
**Behavior**
On YugabyteDB versions 2.14+, we have observed a slow memory growth in workloads that constantly open new connections (rather than reuse long-lived connections for their work).

**Issue** 
PgClientSession expiration logic had a bug - session_expiration_queue_ didn't successfully clean up the expired PgClientSession objects, because of a typo in the comparator, it made it a max heap instead of a min heap. As a result, if the most recent session is still alive, the expired sessions memory would never be reclaimed.

**Fix**
Change the priority queue comparator to make it a min heap, so that the top always has the shortest expiration time, and the expired PgClientSession's memory can always be successfully reclaimed.

issue.body: Jira Link: [DB-3093](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-3093) ### Description When I have many idle postgres connections created the tserver's memory usage increases which is expected but the issue is on termination of these idle connection tserver's memory does not decrease. - The major contributor to tserver's memory increase due to idle connections is coming from read buffers and tcmalloc internals. - Also the read buffer's memory usage decreases on termination of these idle connection but the tserver's memory usage does not decrease and the overall tserver's unaccounted memory increases. - I have seen idle connection's unaccounted memory usage reaching to 1G.
